body:
RAISED BY MYK (2026-07-25, in chat): *"offeredLens is a property of a container, and because a store, an author, even a quarantine are just containers, they all inherit it by default."*

THE GAP, verified. `offeredLens` is a **Gateway OPTION** — `GatewayOptions.offeredLens?: Term` (`src/gateway/gateway.ts:148`), trial-evaluated once at construction to prove it selects a dset (`:303-307`), and read out of `gw.options` on every call by `offeredDeltasImpl` (`src/gateway/ingest.ts:167`). So what a store offers a peer is fixed PER STORE, at open time. Three things follow, and the third is the one that matters:

- A container cannot say what IT offers, so container-to-container federation has no way to express an offer scope. The wall's seeding edge only ever pulls `gw.offeredDeltas()` (`container.ts:922`) — the PRIMARY's store-wide lens — and then narrows INBOUND with its own membership. Outbound-from-a-container does not exist.
- The §28.6 ADMISSION axis has the same shape of gap from the other side: `containerAdmission(reactor, operator, container)` is implemented (`container.ts:514`, `readTrustPolicyAt` filed at the container entity) and is called by NOTHING in `src/` — only `src/index.ts`'s re-export and two tests. `federateImpl` consults `admitForImpl`, which reads the ROOT policy at `loam:trust` and nothing else (`ingest.ts:105-110`). So BOTH sides of container-to-container federation are declared-but-unenforced today, and this ticket should fix them together or say why not.
- **`offeredLens` IS CONFIG, NOT DATA.** No delta, no author, no latest-wins, no negation, no audit trail of what this store offered when. Everything else in this neighbourhood is data — trust (§8), budgets (§25), a container's own knobs as claims about it (§27.1) — and this one option is the exception. Making it a container knob is therefore not just a scoping change; it is the change that makes the offer scope negatable and auditable like everything else.

SHAPE (recommendation, to be argued in the landing PR's spec section): a new optional role on the `loam.container` declaration alongside `membership`/`membershipAt` — inline canonical-JSON Term or a `termClaims` content address, refusing both-at-once exactly as membership does. Adding an OPTIONAL role does not alter the bytes or roles of any delta an older store already holds, so **no §20 migration is owed** — a store predating this simply carries no such role and offers everything, which is today's behavior. State that reasoning explicitly in the PR; it is the kind of claim that should never be implied.

AND THEN THE RAMIFICATION MYK RAISED, which this ticket settles AS PROSE because the architecture has already answered most of it: what does it mean to NARROW a federation policy? **There are three different narrowings with three different costs, and only one of them is retroactive.** Getting this written down is most of the ticket's value.

**1. THE DOOR** (`admitFor` / `loam:trust`, and after this ticket a container's own admission) — FUTURE-ONLY and cheap. It cannot be retroactive: admission is a WRITE-TIME gate (`federateImpl` admits or rejects per delta as it arrives), so deltas already admitted are simply in the store. Nothing about narrowing the door removes them.

   ONE CORRECTION TO THE FRAMING, and it is the half that matters: it is NOT simply "latest-wins on the declaration." The MODE is latest-wins, but the ROSTER is the **UNION of `admit-author` pointers across ALL surviving declarations** — *"a fresh declaration only ADDS; removal is negation (strike the declaration that admitted them)"* (`src/gateway/trust.ts:91-98`). So widening a door is a new delta; NARROWING a roster is a NEGATION of the declaration that admitted the author. Both are deltas, so the change is still data — but a re-declaration cannot narrow, and a design that assumes it can will silently keep admitting.

**2. THE LENS** (a Schema's Policies and masks, `dataStruck`'s striker mask, an author-rank predicate, `offeredLens` itself) — **RETROACTIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, free, and reversible.** It changes what RESOLVES without touching the ground: masks and `select` narrow the operand set a reader evaluates over, the deltas never move, and widening the lens again brings the claims back because they never left. This is the honest answer to "narrow as of the past," and for a registered Schema it is already built and already data (a registration is a delta; latest-per-lens wins).

   THE CORRECTION: for `offeredLens` it is NOT yet reversible-as-data, for the reason above — it is an open-time option, so re-widening means re-opening the gateway. That is precisely what this ticket fixes, and it is the argument for fixing it: the narrowing that is supposed to be the cheap, reversible, retroactive one is today the only one that requires a restart. (A note on `lawfulStrikersJson` specifically, since it is easy to over-read: it is a module-private trust-mask predicate deciding WHOSE NEGATIONS BIND, behind `governedGatherBody`/`tenantSchemaFor`/`dataStruck` — a lens over suppression, not a visibility rank. Cite it for what it is.)

**3. THE MEMBERSHIP** (a stricter rule over the same ground) — and here is the key correction, worth stating loudly *because* log-and-projection thinking makes "replay" the intuitive verb and badly overprices it: **this is not a replay, it is a RE-PROJECTION.** Union is a SET operation and order-independent, so there is no history to re-run — there is only a Term to evaluate once. That is literally what the code does: `selectImpl` is one `evalTerm(parsed, gw.reactor.snapshot())` (`ingest.ts:183`), and `openWall`'s `memberAdmit` computes the member set once per pulse (`container.ts:912-919`). Price it honestly, though: it is ONE PASS over the surviving ground (H8's full-scan shape, and the reason to say so is that it is the cost that scales), not O(offered set) in the sense of something smaller than the store, and in a grow-only store the ground and the history are the same set. What is NOT paid is the sequential re-execution of state transitions, which is what "replay" would mean and what does not exist here.

   A SECOND CORRECTION, in the cheap direction: **a narrowing does not require a new container.** Trust and posture are the only immutable knobs; *"every other knob is latest-wins"* (§27.1), and `readContainerTable` binds the LATEST surviving declaration's membership (`container.ts:439-457`). So re-declaring an EXISTING container with a stricter membership re-projects THE SAME entity, retroactively, for one delta. A fresh container under a new name is needed only when both rules must coexist — the wider one still readable beside the narrower.

**4. AND IF THE BYTES MUST ACTUALLY GO** rather than merely stop resolving: that is ERASURE — operator-only (`erase.ts:115`), per-delta, tombstoned, byte-verified. Not a policy change, and the distinction is the whole of §28.4's ratchet argument: *"you cannot retroactively achieve isolation over grow-only shared ground."*

TWO HONEST CONSEQUENCES TO RECORD, neither of them a defect:

- A re-projected container that is FROZEN has a DIFFERENT ModuleVersion address — the address is a hash over the sorted member ids and deliberately nothing else (`src/gateway/container-identity.ts`), so a different member set is a different name. §27.2 working exactly as designed: you cannot change what a version contains without minting a different version. (Note that the declaration's own `version` role is a provenance citation with *"no runtime effect yet"* — `container.ts:62` — so it does not make a narrowing harder.)
- Because the store is grow-only you get **"the same ground under a stricter rule," never "the wider version never existed."** The old declaration is in the history, negated or superseded, and readable. That is the property, not the price.

FINALLY, THE RAIL THIS TICKET CANNOT SKIP: **a re-projection is a NARROWING, so it owes the negation closure** (H1 — `negated(d, D)` ranges over the OPERAND SET, so a filter that keeps a claim and drops its retraction hands the reader a live retracted claim). `containerScopeImpl` and the `membership` branch of `memberAdmit` already carry `withNegationClosure`. **The `admit`-predicate branch still does not:** `container.ts:913` is `if (spec.membership === undefined) return base === undefined ? undefined : base;` — the caller's raw predicate, unclosed, exactly as T43 reports (T43 cites `quarantine-pool.ts:86`; T32's lifting moved that body into `container.ts` while `quarantine-pool.ts` remains as the preset wrapper, so T43's line reference is stale but its finding is live). T43 also owns the FEDERATION INBOUND door, which is the same hole on the receiving side and is directly in this ticket's path — an offer scope is worthless if the receiver's admit drops the retractions the offer carried. **So this ticket depends on T43**, and it should not invent a second closure beside the one T43 lands.

CARE: it widens what a container declaration can SAY and what the federation door reads, which decides rather than repairs — **Myk's merge (P6)**. The PR states in one line what a container may now express that it could not before. No migration is owed (an added optional role changes no existing delta's bytes), and the PR should say so rather than leave it inferred.

HALF-OVERTAKEN (stale sweep, 2026-08-25) — read this before building: The 'container-to-container federation cannot exist / has no outbound path' half died to §46 (PRs #434/#440: channels, pools, receiver-owned names), and the container-scoped outbound offer now converges with the T188/T196 remaining halves headed into the T230 offer-token ticket (src/federation/channel.ts's own refusal text names that line). The core gap lives on main: offeredLens is still an open-time GatewayOptions option (src/gateway/gateway.ts:213, read from gw.options at src/gateway/ingest.ts:310), no loam.container offer role exists, and containerAdmission (container.ts:645) is still called by nothing in src/ but the index re-export.
title: `offeredLens` is a property of a CONTAINER, not of a Gateway — and the three narrowings, only one of which is retroactive
